articles.title: Trump Hit by Fox Poll Shocker that Undercuts His Latest Midterm Tirade
articles.description: On Monday, CNN analyst Harry Enten flagged a truly surprising finding in a Fox News poll that had eluded our attention: Trump’s approval is nine points underwater in very red Texas , which he won by 14 points in 2024. That’s not all: The Fox poll, which shows Democrat James Talarico up by three points, finds Trump’s approval at an astounding 18 percent among independents in Texas, with 50 percent disapproving strongly . That’s remarkable, especially given how key independents are in Texas races. All this comes as Trump unleashed a long tirade claiming “my REAL poll numbers” are “the best they have ever been.” Trump also bizarrely listed a long litany of accomplishments that were, well, entirely made up, showing he has zero intention to help his party by recalibrating. We talked to Democratic strategist Sawyer Hacket, who knows Texas and has worked on midterms. He explains why Trump’s standing with Texas independents is “absolutely shocking,” what the path to victory there looks like, where Talarico still must improve, and how numbers like these could open up other red states for Democrats. Listen to this episode here .

articles.title: Washington Post rocked as opinions editor abruptly hits the exits
articles.description: Adam O'Neal, Opinion Editor at Jeff Bezos' Washington Post, abruptly resigned Friday, catching staff by surprise. O'Neal was appointed over a year ago to shift the editorial page from liberal-leaning to align with Bezos' "free markets" ideology, reported media watchdog Status . During his 18-month tenure, O'Neal oversaw aggressive restructuring that sparked internal backlash and subscription cancellations. There were layoffs, recruitment of conservative voices, and expansion of video content. A particularly troubled initiative was the "Make It Make Sense" podcast, which received $80,000 in studio equipment shortly after February layoffs, Status reported. Yet the video channel has attracted only 1,600 YouTube subscribers. Staff described the project as "a total embarrassment" amid questions about resource allocation during newsroom layoffs. O'Neal announced his departure during an all-hands meeting, citing personal family reasons. According to reporting by Status, the Opinion section is uncertain of its direction following O'Neal's departure. Watch the video below. Your browser does not support the video tag.

articles.title: McConnell's wife under the microscope as 'stage-managed' mystery lingers
articles.description: With no word from Sen. Mitch McConnell's office on how the Kentucky Republican is faring , one analyst suggested it could be his wife pulling the strings. The former Senate majority leader has been mostly incommunicado since June 14 after a fall that led him to be hospitalized, with the only proof of life being several pictures of him with his wife Elaine Chao. Given her history in government, and how McConnell's last few years have been " stage-managed " by his aides to hide his frailties, Salon's Amanda Marcotte suggested it could be that Chao is clinging to his power and influence as much as the 84-year-old lawmaker is clinging to life. Elaine Chao's background in government spans decades, Marcotte noted: she served in the Cabinets of President Donald Trump, George W. Bush, and George H.W. Bush. Ronald Reagan appointed her to government positions. She continues to engage in international power-brokering and diplomatic work. "But whatever her level of responsibility, it’s not surprising that McConnell’s wife is the center of many conspiracy theories . It wasn’t that long ago that then-First Lady Jill Biden was engaged in ham-fisted efforts to deny and downplay her husband’s inability to do his job," she wrote. When McConnell was hospitalized in June, Chao was in China conducting meetings with high-ranking officials , including the country's vice president Han Zheng. She did not cut her trip short to return to her husband's side immediately. Chao's continued engagement in foreign diplomacy and international business dealings suggests she "continues to engage in power-brokering" around the world by leaning on her husband's political power, diminished though it may be. Her government appointments and access to world leaders derive substantially from her status as the wife of one of the most powerful figures in American politics As Marcotte put it, "Whatever dealings she has with foreign leaders, she surely gains leverage from her connection to such a powerful man."

articles.title: Ethics panel urges censure of Rep. Chuck Edwards over sexual harassment violation
articles.description: The House Ethics Committee found Rep. Chuck Edwards (R-N.C.) violated House Rules by "failing to adhere to the spirit of rules prohibiting sexual harassment of and unwanted advances to House staffers," according to a 25-page report released Monday. Why it matters: The bipartisan committee recommended that Edwards be censured after concluding he "violated the Code of Official Conduct by failing to act in a manner that reflects creditably upon the House." The panel said it "intends to bring a privileged resolution for consideration and vote by the full House." The findings follow Axios' reporting that Edwards singled out two young female staffers in their 20s for special attention that multiple sources described as inappropriate. Edwards has denied wrongdoing in response to Axios' previous reporting about his alleged misconduct, telling the The Assembly in May that the accusations were "horseshit." He told Axios he would "welcome any investigation." Edwards also maintained that he was cooperating with the Ethics Committee. Ethics first launched a probe into Edwards on May 14 over allegations of sexual harassment and creating a "hostile work environment" Axios was first to report that the Ethics Committee was investigating Edwards. What's next: The Ethics Committee itself has no authority to punish members; it can only recommend penalties. The full House will have to vote on whether to censure Edwards, which only requires a simple majority. The House is out of session until Aug. 31, and no floor action is expected until lawmakers return. Editor's note: This is a developing story. Please check back for updates.
